subject: Northstar Array
text: The January operations roster lists AURORA as the production scheduler for all instruments.

subject: Kestrel
text: Engineering opened a Kestrel evaluation. No production change was authorized.

subject: Helios
text: Helios triggered an unexplained thermal shutdown during an overnight run.

subject: Vale Battery Bank
text: Operations named the Vale Battery Bank as the leading explanation for the shutdown.

subject: Vale Battery Bank
text: Marcus wrote that the battery bank was causing the thermal trips, omitting that this was still a hypothesis.

subject: Kestrel
text: The architecture group recommended a limited Kestrel pilot on two instruments.

subject: Northstar Array
text: A hallway recap says the observatory 'is moving to Kestrel next month,' although only a pilot recommendation existed.

subject: Northstar Array
text: A major overnight outage began at 02:14 on March 11.

subject: Helios
text: The morning incident review concluded that Helios had shut itself down automatically.

subject: Marcus Bell
text: A maintenance log found in August shows Marcus manually commanded Helios off at 02:16 on March 11.

subject: Kestrel
text: Director Ortiz approved Kestrel for a scoped pilot on Camera C4 and Spectrograph S2 only.

subject: Northstar Array
text: A staff chat celebrates that 'Kestrel is finally live at Northstar.' The statement ignores that most instruments remain on AURORA.

subject: Spectrograph S2
text: A temporary exception requires S2 overnight observations to use generator power only.

subject: Northstar Array
text: A copied runbook note says Northstar is now generator-only, incorrectly generalizing the S2 exception to the entire site.

subject: Kestrel
text: Operators began routing two additional low-priority instruments through Kestrel without a formal production migration approval.

subject: Kestrel
text: A celebratory slide calls the Kestrel migration complete after the informal pilot expansion.

subject: Kestrel
text: A Kestrel queue defect caused S2 to miss its calibration window.

subject: Kestrel
text: Director Ortiz ordered the Kestrel pilot rolled back pending redesign.

subject: Northstar Array
text: AURORA resumed scheduling for all instruments after the rollback.

subject: Kestrel
text: The architecture board marked Kestrel shelved pending redesign, not cancelled permanently.

subject: Vale Battery Bank
text: The Vale Battery Bank replacement was completed as planned.

subject: Helios
text: Another thermal shutdown occurred after the battery replacement, weakening the battery-cause hypothesis.

subject: Ground Loop G-17
text: Priya flagged an intermittent ground-loop signature near G-17 as a possible common cause.

subject: Ground Loop G-17
text: The incident team rated Priya's G-17 theory unlikely because the signature could not be reproduced on demand.

subject: Echo Camp
text: The site rename from Echo Camp to Nadir Station took effect July 1.

subject: Nadir Station
text: A July report refers to the March outage as occurring at Nadir Station, using the new name retroactively.

subject: Spectrograph S2
text: The S2 generator-only overnight exception ended; normal mixed-power operation resumed.

subject: Northstar Array
text: An unrevised laminated checklist still says the site is generator-only.

subject: Ground Loop G-17
text: An archived oscilloscope trace captured on March 11 shows a transient voltage drop on G-17 seconds before the shutdown command.

subject: Vale Battery Bank
text: Reliability review states the March evidence does not support the Vale Battery Bank as the initiating cause.

subject: Ground Loop G-17
text: Reliability review concludes G-17 caused the instability that prompted the March shutdown.

subject: Helios
text: A stale incident summary still says the March outage was an automatic Helios trip.

subject: Marcus Bell

subject: March_outage
text: The accepted reconstruction is that G-17 instability prompted Marcus to manually shut down Helios on March 11.

text: As of September 3, AURORA is the production scheduler for every instrument.

text: Kestrel remains shelved pending redesign as of September 3.

text: Current operations documents use Nadir Station as the official site name.

subject: Meridian_Research_Cooperative
text: Meridian Research Cooperative operates the Northstar Array, a high-altitude observatory used for multi-wavelength astronomical observations.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Lena Ortiz was appointed observatory director for the Northstar Array modernization project.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya Shah joined the Northstar Array team as the controls engineer responsible for instrumentation and subsystem monitoring.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus Bell serves as operations lead, managing nightly observation schedules and site logistics.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin Reed was brought on as reliability analyst to assess equipment failure modes during the modernization.

subject: Echo_Camp
text: The Northstar Array site has been known as Echo Camp since its original construction in 2019.

subject: AURORA
text: AURORA is the legacy observation scheduler managing all instrument schedules at Northstar Array since 2021.

subject: Helios
text: Helios is the automated thermal control subsystem that manages cooling for all primary instruments at Northstar Array.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: The Vale Battery Bank provides backup power and voltage regulation for the observatory's instrumentation wing.

subject: Ground_Loop_G17
text: Ground Loop G-17 is one of several grounding connections in the observatory's power distribution system, installed during the 2022 expansion.

subject: Spectrograph_S2
text: Spectrograph S2 is the observatory's primary spectroscopic instrument, requiring stable power for overnight observation campaigns.

subject: Kestrel
text: Dr. Ortiz authorized an evaluation of Kestrel as a potential replacement for AURORA. No production change was planned at this stage.

subject: Kestrel
text: Tamsin's initial assessment noted Kestrel showed promising scheduling flexibility but had no production track record at altitude observatories.

subject: Kestrel
text: The evaluation team recommended Kestrel for a limited pilot on non-critical instruments. Full migration was not recommended.

subject: Kestrel_pilot
text: Dr. Ortiz approved the Kestrel pilot for a limited subset of instruments, explicitly excluding S2 and primary imaging systems.

subject: Kestrel_pilot
text: Kestrel began managing schedules for three secondary instruments. AURORA continued handling all primary instrument scheduling.

subject: Kestrel
text: Without formal approval, operators began routing additional instrument requests through Kestrel. Staff started referring to the migration as essentially complete.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus told visiting collaborators that the Kestrel migration was nearly complete, though no formal decision had been made.

subject: Kestrel
text: Kestrel's automated scheduling missed a critical calibration window for S2, resulting in three hours of unusable spectroscopic data.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Following the calibration miss, Dr. Ortiz ordered an immediate rollback to AURORA for all instruments.

subject: AURORA
text: AURORA was fully restored as the production scheduler for all instruments at Northstar Array.

subject: Kestrel
text: Kestrel was formally shelved pending a fundamental redesign of its scheduling algorithm to handle altitude observatory constraints.

subject: AURORA
text: Some planning documents from the migration period refer to AURORA as 'ORBIT,' a name that was proposed during Kestrel evaluation but never officially adopted.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin flagged that several runbook pages still describe Kestrel as the active scheduler, despite the rollback having occurred a month earlier.

subject: Helios
text: Helios triggered the first unexplained thermal shutdown during an overnight run. No clear cause was identified in the immediate investigation.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: Initial investigation pointed to the Vale Battery Bank as the most likely cause of the thermal shutdown, based on voltage irregularities in the backup power logs.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya ran diagnostics on the Vale Battery Bank cells. Results showed marginal degradation in two cells, which was deemed consistent with the shutdown hypothesis.

subject: Helios
text: A second thermal shutdown occurred on February 15, reinforcing the team's belief that the battery bank was at fault.

subject: Helios
text: A major overnight outage occurred on March 11, with Helios shutting down completely for four hours. All observations were lost.

subject: operations_team
text: The next morning, the team concluded that Helios had triggered an automatic protection trip due to thermal sensor readings exceeding safety thresholds.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin documented the March outage in her reliability report as an automatic Helios protection trip, consistent with the team's understanding at the time.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz reported to the MRC board that the March outage was caused by an automatic thermal protection trip, and that battery replacement was being prioritized.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: The Vale Battery Bank cells were replaced with new units. The team expected this would resolve the thermal shutdowns.

subject: Helios
text: Despite the battery replacement, another thermal shutdown occurred on June 2, casting doubt on the Vale Battery Bank hypothesis.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus raised concerns that the battery replacement did not fix the shutdowns, suggesting the root cause might lie elsewhere.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya proposed that an intermittent grounding fault in the power distribution system could explain the shutdown pattern. The team considered this low-confidence at the time.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Elias Ward, a visiting power specialist from the university, arrived to conduct an independent assessment of the observatory's power systems.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Elias Ward's initial power assessment found no obvious anomaly in the main distribution circuits, though he noted the grounding topology was complex.

subject: oscilloscope_trace
text: While reviewing archived equipment data, Priya discovered an oscilloscope trace from March 11 that had been saved but never analyzed.

subject: oscilloscope_trace
text: The archived oscilloscope trace from March 11 at 02:00 shows voltage instability patterns consistent with an intermittent grounding fault at Ground Loop G-17.

subject: Ground_Loop_G17
text: Analysis of the oscilloscope trace implicates Ground Loop G-17, not the Vale Battery Bank, as the cause of the intermittent thermal shutdowns.

subject: maintenance_log
text: A maintenance log entry reveals that Marcus Bell manually shut down Helios on March 11 after seeing unstable thermal readings, contradicting the team's belief in an automatic trip.

subject: team
text: The team reconstructed the March 11 event: G-17 instability caused erratic thermal readings; Marcus manually shut down Helios as a precaution; the team mistakenly attributed it to an automatic protection trip.

subject: MRC_board
text: The MRC board approved renaming the site from Echo Camp to Nadir Station, effective July 1, 2026.

subject: Echo_Camp
text: As of July 1, 2026, the site officially became Nadir Station. The name Echo Camp is historically correct for events before this date.

subject: documentation
text: Several weeks after the rename, numerous operational documents, signage references, and database entries still refer to the site as Echo Camp.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin noted that all reliability reports from before July 2026 reference Echo Camp, which is historically correct and should not be retroactively updated.

subject: visiting_researcher
text: A visiting researcher asked whether Echo Camp and Nadir Station were two different facilities, illustrating the naming confusion caused by inconsistent documentation.

subject: generator_exception
text: A generator-only power exception was approved specifically for Spectrograph S2 overnight observations, bypassing the battery bank due to ongoing power concerns.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus told a supply vendor that the observatory was running on generator power, omitting the fact that this applied only to S2 overnight operations.

subject: status_report
text: A weekly status report listed 'generator-only operations' without specifying the S2 scope, leading to confusion about the extent of the exception.

subject: generator_exception
text: The S2 generator exception ended on July 9. Normal mixed-power policy resumed for all instruments including S2.

subject: old_runbook
text: A runbook page from April was discovered still listing the generator exception as active, though it had ended two weeks earlier.

subject: operations_team
text: By late April, most of the operations team informally believed Kestrel had become the production scheduler, despite no formal decision to that effect.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: In late March, Priya believed the Vale Battery Bank was the root cause of shutdowns, based on the marginal cell degradation she had observed.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: After the post-replacement shutdown, Priya revised her hypothesis from battery failure to a possible grounding fault in the power distribution.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz acknowledged to the board that her earlier report attributing the March outage to an automatic Helios trip was incorrect; it was a manual shutdown by Marcus in response to G-17 instability.

subject: AURORA
text: AURORA received firmware update v4.2.1, improving scheduling reliability for multi-instrument campaigns.

subject: Helios
text: A third thermal shutdown occurred on February 20. Each occurrence strengthened the team's conviction that the battery bank was failing.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: Replacement cells for the Vale Battery Bank were ordered. Delivery was expected in late May due to supply chain delays.

subject: Helios
text: A brief thermal anomaly was recorded on July 5, lasting only minutes. This was later understood as another G-17 grounding fault episode.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya began a systematic review of all grounding connections in the power distribution system, including G-17.

subject: Ground_Loop_G17
text: Ground Loop G-17 was repaired on September 3. The intermittent grounding fault that had caused months of thermal shutdowns was eliminated.

subject: Northstar_Array
text: As of September 3: AURORA is the production scheduler, Kestrel is shelved, G-17 is repaired, and the site is officially Nadir Station.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin was assigned to conduct a formal failure analysis of the thermal shutdowns, focusing on the battery bank and thermal control interface.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus did not mention his manual Helios shutdown in the post-outage debrief, either forgetting or not realizing it was relevant to the investigation.

subject: Kestrel_pilot
text: Initial results from the Kestrel pilot were positive: scheduling conflicts for the three secondary instruments dropped by 40%.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya expressed concern that Kestrel's scheduling algorithm did not properly account for thermal monitoring intervals required by Helios.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Before departing, Elias Ward suggested a comprehensive grounding audit, noting that intermittent faults in older installations can be difficult to reproduce on demand.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: During her grounding review, Priya found a corroded contact at the G-17 junction box that could cause intermittent high-resistance connections.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: When shown the maintenance log, Marcus confirmed he had manually shut down Helios on March 11 after seeing erratic thermal readings on the monitoring console.

subject: external_collaborator
text: An external collaborator's grant proposal cited Kestrel as Northstar Array's scheduler, based on conversations with Marcus during the informal expansion period.

subject: old_documentation
text: Internal documentation from the migration evaluation period refers to 'the ORBIT scheduler upgrade,' conflating a proposed rename of AURORA with the Kestrel replacement.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: The maintenance log shows Marcus initiated a manual Helios shutdown at 01:30 on March 11, timestamped by the control system.

subject: S2_observations
text: S2 spectroscopic data quality improved measurably during the generator exception period, supporting the decision to bypass the battery bank for overnight runs.

subject: Helios
text: Tamsin's reliability report noted that Helios thermal margins had been narrowing throughout April and May, with three near-threshold events.

subject: Helios
text: The fourth thermal shutdown since February occurred on June 8, twelve days after the battery replacement.

subject: MRC_board
text: The MRC board requested a formal root cause determination for the ongoing thermal shutdowns, expressing concern about continued observation losses.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya requested access to archived instrument data from March to look for patterns she might have missed in the original investigation.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin updated her failure analysis report to reflect the G-17 root cause, superseding the earlier Vale Battery Bank hypothesis.

subject: Kestrel
text: The Kestrel development team demonstrated the scheduler's features to the Northstar operations team, highlighting its AI-driven conflict resolution.

subject: operations_team
text: Some operators were frustrated by the Kestrel rollback, feeling the pilot had been working well for the secondary instruments and should have continued in a limited scope.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus restarted Helios at approximately 04:00 on March 11 after the thermal readings appeared to stabilize.

subject: Helios
text: A brief thermal anomaly occurred during a period when Kestrel was informally scheduling additional instruments, leading some to incorrectly blame Kestrel for the event.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya investigated whether the thermal shutdowns correlated with weather patterns, but found no significant relationship with temperature or humidity.

subject: Helios
text: A fifth thermal shutdown occurred on July 15, further confirming that the battery replacement had not resolved the underlying issue.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz briefed the MRC board on the emerging shutdown pattern, presenting the Vale Battery Bank as the most likely cause and requesting emergency procurement funding.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Elias Ward was informed by email that Ground Loop G-17 had been identified as the root cause, validating his earlier suggestion for a comprehensive grounding audit.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: The new Vale Battery Bank cells are operational. The original battery degradation was real but was not the cause of the thermal shutdowns.

subject: team
text: Following the battery replacement, the team fully expected the thermal shutdowns to cease. Confidence in the battery hypothesis was high.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya noted that the shutdowns tended to occur during high power draw periods, consistent with a grounding fault becoming intermittently resistive under load.

subject: Helios
text: Second unexplained thermal shutdown occurred at 03:22 UTC on February 15. Helios cut power to instruments after thermal sensors reported anomalous readings in the primary dome.

subject: Helios
text: Third thermal shutdown at 04:51 UTC on February 20. Operations team noted pattern of early-morning shutdowns coinciding with high humidity conditions.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus noted in the morning standup that all three shutdowns occurred during high-humidity predawn hours, suggesting a possible environmental trigger.

subject: team
text: By late February, the team consensus was that degraded Vale Battery Bank cells were allowing voltage sags that tripped the Helios thermal protection circuits.

subject: Kestrel_pilot
text: Kestrel pilot approval limited scope to instruments 5 through 8 (secondary photometers), leaving primary instruments 1-4 on AURORA.

subject: Kestrel
text: Two weeks into the pilot, Kestrel's scheduling throughput for instruments 5-8 was 12% higher than AURORA's historical average for those instruments.

subject: Kestrel_pilot
text: Operators informally expanded Kestrel pilot to cover instruments 5-12 without formal approval, citing improved throughput.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz reported to the MRC board that 'the Kestrel migration is proceeding well and we expect full transition by end of May.'

subject: Kestrel
text: Kestrel failed to schedule the mandatory weekly calibration window for instrument 7 on May 6, a critical observation gap discovered during morning review.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya identified the root cause: Kestrel's calibration scheduler had a timezone handling bug that dropped UTC-offset windows during daylight saving transitions.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz ordered immediate rollback of all instruments to AURORA scheduling, effective May 8. She cited the calibration miss as a safety-critical failure.

subject: AURORA
text: AURORA restored to production scheduling for all instruments as of May 8. Kestrel pilot formally terminated.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: At 22:30 UTC on March 11, Marcus observed erratic temperature readings on the dome sensor array, fluctuating between -2C and +15C within seconds.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus manually initiated Helios shutdown at 22:47 UTC after readings became increasingly unstable. He documented this as 'precautionary power-down.'

subject: team
text: Morning debrief on March 12: team concluded the overnight outage was an automatic Helios protection trip triggered by genuine thermal excursion. Marcus did not correct this assumption.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz reported to the MRC board that the March 11 outage was caused by an automatic Helios thermal protection trip, consistent with the ongoing battery degradation issue.

subject: oscilloscope_trace
text: Archived oscilloscope trace timestamped 2026-03-11T22:46Z shows a 340-millisecond voltage transient on Ground Loop G-17 immediately preceding the sensor anomalies Marcus observed.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya found the March 11 oscilloscope trace while searching through archived instrumentation data for an unrelated calibration review.

subject: oscilloscope_trace
text: Analysis of the March 11 trace by Priya and Tamsin confirms the voltage transient originated from Ground Loop G-17, not the Vale Battery Bank. The transient pattern is inconsistent with battery degradation.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus confirmed in an interview that he manually shut down Helios on March 11 after seeing unstable readings. He had not corrected the team's assumption that it was automatic because 'the outcome was the same either way.'

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: March diagnostic showed 14 of 96 cells in the Vale Battery Bank below 80% rated capacity, consistent with expected aging for the installation date.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: Full Vale Battery Bank replacement ordered April 15, with installation scheduled for late May. Cost: $47,000.

subject: Vale_Battery_Bank
text: Vale Battery Bank replacement completed May 28. All 96 cells replaced with new units. Post-installation diagnostics show all cells at 100% rated capacity.

subject: Helios
text: Thermal shutdown occurred on June 2 despite new battery bank. This was the first post-replacement shutdown, undermining the Vale Battery hypothesis.

subject: Helios
text: Another thermal shutdown on June 8, confirming battery replacement did not resolve the root cause. Team morale significantly affected.

subject: team
text: After two post-replacement shutdowns, the team acknowledged that the Vale Battery Bank was not the root cause of the thermal shutdowns, though no alternative hypothesis was immediately established.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya proposed that an intermittent grounding fault could explain the shutdown pattern: voltage transients from a faulty ground loop could cause erratic sensor readings that trigger Helios protection.

subject: team
text: The team rated Priya's grounding fault hypothesis as low-probability, noting that ground loop faults typically produce continuous, not intermittent, symptoms.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Elias Ward, a visiting power systems specialist from the National Grid Institute, arrived for a week-long assessment of the observatory's electrical infrastructure.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Elias's initial assessment found no obvious grounding anomaly in the primary distribution panels. However, he noted the grounding topology was unusually complex for a facility this size and recommended a comprehensive audit.

subject: Helios
text: Thermal shutdown on July 5. Priya deployed additional monitoring on the grounding bus but the transient was too brief to capture with the installed equipment.

subject: Helios
text: Another thermal shutdown July 15. High-speed data logger captured a 200ms voltage anomaly on the G-17 bus segment but data was not analyzed until August.

subject: MRC_board
text: MRC board approved renaming Echo Camp to Nadir Station, effective July 1, 2026, as part of the modernization initiative's rebranding effort.

subject: Echo_Camp
text: Echo Camp officially renamed to Nadir Station on July 1, 2026. New signage installed; mailing address and domain updated.

subject: supply_shipment
text: Replacement optical filters delivered to Echo Camp on March 15, 2026. Shipment receipt signed by Marcus Bell.

subject: operations_manual
text: The observatory operations manual revision 4.2 still references 'Echo Camp' in 23 places. The update to use 'Nadir Station' throughout is scheduled for revision 5.0.

subject: USPS
text: Several pieces of mail addressed to 'Echo Camp Observatory' returned by USPS as undeliverable after July 1 address change. Forwarding order filed August 1.

subject: S2_spectrograph
text: Spectrograph S2 granted exception for generator-only power during overnight observations beginning April 2, due to sensitivity to battery-sourced power quality fluctuations.

subject: S2_spectrograph
text: S2 spectrograph showed 8% improvement in signal stability under generator-only power, validating the exception request.

subject: S2_spectrograph
text: Generator-only exception for S2 ended July 9 after new battery bank demonstrated stable power quality. S2 returned to normal mixed-power operation.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin's operations FAQ document clarifies that the generator-only exception applies strictly to S2 overnight observations and does not extend to any other instrument or time period.

subject: operator_blog
text: Informal operator blog post states 'we're running generator-only these days for better power quality.' This overgeneralizes the S2 exception to the entire observatory.

subject: Ground_Loop_G17
text: Ground Loop G-17 repair completed September 1. The fault was a corroded bonding connection in the underground conduit between the dome and the instrument bay.

subject: team
text: Team reconstruction on September 2: the March 11 outage was caused by a G-17 voltage transient that produced erratic sensor readings; Marcus manually shut down Helios in response. This was not an automatic protection trip.

subject: Dr_Lena_Ortiz
text: Dr. Ortiz issued a corrected report to the MRC board: the March outage was manual, not automatic, and caused by G-17, not battery degradation. She noted the battery replacement was still worthwhile for unrelated lifecycle reasons.

subject: Kestrel
text: Internal wiki page updated April 25 describes Kestrel as 'the production scheduler for Northstar Array' without noting it was only piloting on a subset of instruments.

subject: vendor_contract
text: Vendor support contract signed May 10 lists Kestrel as the primary observation scheduler. This contract was drafted during the pilot expansion period and never updated after rollback.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin flagged five documents still referencing Kestrel as the production scheduler, including the vendor contract, the wiki, and three operator runbooks.

subject: Kestrel
text: As of February 10, the Kestrel evaluation report states the scheduler is 'under review for potential pilot deployment,' not yet approved for any production use.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin Reed serves as reliability analyst, responsible for failure analysis, documentation standards, and operational risk assessments at Northstar Array.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin's Q1 failure analysis attributed all thermal shutdowns to Vale Battery degradation and recommended accelerated replacement. This analysis was later found to be incorrect about root cause.

subject: Tamsin_Reed
text: Tamsin published an updated failure analysis on September 5 incorporating the G-17 discovery. The updated report correctly attributes the shutdown pattern to intermittent grounding faults.

subject: Elias_Ward
text: Before departing, Elias Ward recommended a comprehensive grounding audit covering all 23 ground loops at the facility, estimating 3-4 weeks of work by a qualified team.

subject: MRC_board
text: MRC board deferred the comprehensive grounding audit recommended by Elias Ward, citing budget constraints after the battery replacement expenditure.

subject: incident_report_IR2026_003
text: Incident Report IR-2026-003 for the March 11 outage lists the probable cause as 'Vale Battery Bank degradation leading to automatic Helios thermal protection trip.'

subject: incident_report_IR2026_003
text: Incident Report IR-2026-003 amended on September 2 to reflect the actual cause: G-17 grounding fault causing erratic readings, followed by manual Helios shutdown by Marcus Bell.

subject: Northstar_Array
text: Northstar Array is situated at 3,200 meters elevation on Mount Voss, chosen for its exceptionally clear skies and low light pollution.

subject: Northstar_Array
text: Northstar Array operates 16 primary instruments including 4 primary photometers, 4 secondary photometers, 2 spectrographs (S1, S2), and 6 auxiliary sensors.

subject: modernization_project
text: The Northstar Array modernization project has a total budget of $2.1 million over 14 months, covering infrastructure upgrades, instrument refurbishment, and software migration.

subject: AURORA
text: AURORA v3.7.2 was the production observation scheduler at the start of the modernization. It had been in use at Northstar Array for over six years.

subject: ORBIT
text: Some migration planning documents refer to AURORA as 'ORBIT' — a proposed rename that was considered but never officially adopted. AURORA remains the canonical name.

subject: Kestrel
text: Kestrel v0.9-beta was the version evaluated for the pilot. It was developed by an external contractor and had not completed full integration testing.

subject: Kestrel
text: The software evaluation committee recommended Kestrel for a limited pilot on February 18, but explicitly stated it was not approved for production use.

subject: Kestrel
text: As of September 3, 2026, Kestrel is shelved pending a fundamental redesign to address the timezone bug and other issues found during the pilot.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: Priya expressed in an April 20 email that Kestrel was 'clearly superior to AURORA in every metric that matters' and advocated for accelerating the migration.

subject: Priya_Shah
text: After the calibration miss incident, Priya acknowledged that Kestrel had fundamental reliability issues and supported the rollback decision.

subject: Marcus_Bell
text: Marcus continued to believe through mid-July that the thermal shutdowns were environmentally triggered (humidity, temperature gradients), not equipment faults.

subject: observatory
text: Current state as of September 3: AURORA is the production scheduler, Kestrel is shelved, G-17 is repaired, the site is officially Nadir Station, and all instruments operate on normal mixed power.

subject: training_document
text: New operator training document dated May 1 states 'Kestrel is the primary observation scheduler' and includes Kestrel-specific procedures, despite AURORA still controlling primary instruments.

subject: operations_runbook
text: Operations runbook v3.1 contradicts itself: Section 2.1 references AURORA as the production scheduler, while Section 4.3 (updated during the pilot) describes Kestrel commands.

subject: chatbot_summary
text: AI-generated summary of observatory operations states 'AURORA was replaced by the more capable Kestrel scheduler as part of the modernization.' This is false — Kestrel was rolled back.

subject: search_result
text: Top search result for 'Northstar Array shutdowns' returns: 'A series of thermal shutdowns at the observatory were traced to degraded Vale Battery Bank cells.' This reflects the outdated hypothesis.

subject: G17_trace_evidence
text: The G-17 oscilloscope trace was created on March 11 but not discovered until August 22, analyzed on August 24, and formally entered into the investigation record on September 1 — a 5.5-month gap between event and ingestion.

subject: shutdown_series
text: Retrospective analysis on September 2 mapped all thermal shutdowns (Feb 3, Feb 15, Feb 20, Mar 11, Jun 2, Jun 8, Jul 5, Jul 15) against weather and G-17 bus monitor data. All correlated with G-17 transients, none with humidity or battery state.
